shouldFix.title: terminalStatusCheck's legacy exemption is triggered by absence rather than identity, and its enumeration is already incomplete against four governed lanes in the artifact's own register
evidence: The clause reads: 'If the pinned file has reviewStatus or reviewState, it MUST be COMPLETE or COMPLETED before the verdict is eligible for registration; any other present status REFUSES. If both members are absent, the file is a legacy verdict-only schema (Claude/Codex v8; Claude v10; Claude v12) and is eligible on verdict alone. Do not infer COMPLETE from the register field.' The branch is entered on a structural condition, both members absent, while the parenthetical asserts an identity, that the file is one of four named lanes.

The rule has no lower version bound. registerCoverageRule.when reads only 'whenever a successor register entry for round N is authored', and honestyRepairsKeyRule states that 'predecessorVerdictFindings is maintained from v6 onward'. Only the FromVN obligation is separately scoped 'for v8 onward'. So v6 and v7 register entries are governed by provenanceCheck and terminalStatusCheck.

Four governed lanes enter the legacy branch and are not among the four named. I read every pinned lane file from v6 through v20 and checked both members: v6/claude2, v6/codex, v7/claude2 and v7/codex all have reviewStatus and reviewState absent, exactly as the four named lanes do. All four are full register entries carrying path, sha256 and verdict, so they are subject to the rule rather than incidental.

Both available readings of the clause yield a defect. If the parenthetical defines the legacy set, the clause misstates its own corpus, since eight governed lanes take the branch while it names four. If the parenthetical is illustrative and the operative trigger is absence, the exemption is open-ended and any future verdict file that omits both members is eligible on verdict alone.

The open-ended reading is the shape that has failed twice in this artifact. At v17 an unrecognized schema extracted the empty set rather than refusing, and at v18 a skipped severity key was refused only when it happened to be a positive integer. Both were structural conditions standing in for an identity the rule meant to name, and both were repaired by making the rule total rather than conditional.

Codex's frozen requiredRepair anticipated this in terms: 'Keep legacy-schema handling explicit rather than inferring acceptance from the register field.' v21 keeps the enumeration explicit in prose but leaves the trigger inferential, so a file qualifies by what it lacks rather than by being a known legacy artifact.

The live corpus is clean, which bounds this to SHOULD-FIX. Implementing provenanceCheck, terminalStatusCheck, verdictConsistencyCheck, laneCheck, pairCheck, dispositionCheck, idCheck and the extractor exactly as written and running them over every lane from v6 through v20 produces zero failures: every path exists, every recorded digest reproduces, every recorded verdict equals its pinned file's verdict, no present status is anything but COMPLETE, and no lane records ACCEPT while carrying a blocking finding.
shouldFix.impact: terminalStatusCheck exists so that a verdict is registrable only once its review is terminal, which is the guard against recording an in-progress or abandoned review as a round's outcome. As written, a file becomes exempt from that guard by omitting two members, and the artifact's own register already contains four lanes the enumeration does not cover, so the clause cannot be read as a closed allowlist. A future reviewer file that carries a verdict but omits both status members, which is precisely what an interrupted or non-conforming writer produces, is eligible on verdict alone; the check that would have caught it is the one the absence disables.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Make legacy eligibility an identity rather than an absence. Pin the legacy set explicitly by digest, which costs nothing because every qualifying file already carries a sha256 in the register, and require that a file with both status members absent be eligible on verdict alone only if its digest is on that list, refusing otherwise. Extend the list to the eight lanes that actually qualify, adding v6/claude2, v6/codex, v7/claude2 and v7/codex to the four already named, or state an explicit version bound if v6 and v7 are meant to be outside registerCoverageRule's scope.

advisories.title: v21 changes nothing outside the review-bookkeeping machinery, continuing a nine-generation pattern in which the host-effect authorization substance is untouched
advisories.observation: I diffed v20 against v21 across every leaf path and partitioned the result. Excluding the register, the repair arrays, the coverage and extractor and id rules, recordedInputs and the succession metadata, the number of substantive paths that changed is zero, with no removals anywhere. The same holds generation over generation since v13: every finding repaired at v14 through v21 has been about predecessorVerdictFindings, honestyRepairsFromVN, frozenReviewFindingExtractor, registerCoverageRule, findingIdRule or the disposition vocabulary. The authorization content itself, failClosed's six conjuncts, coveredActs and its class gates, the authorizationRecord schema, effectCommit, outcomeVocabulary and joinBlockerDisposition, is unchanged and still carries BLK-1 through BLK-4 as STILL-ROUTED.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: This is an observation about where review effort has gone, not a defect in the artifact. The bookkeeping findings have all been real, including two of mine and six of Codex's, and the substantive content was independently examined and found coherent at v16 and again at v19 across failClosed, coveredActs, outcomeVocabulary, effectCommit and the join blockers. Nothing has regressed. I record it because a coordinator deciding whether this contract is converging on DR-105 and DR-114 would want to know that nine consecutive generations moved only the self-review apparatus, and because the artifact has grown from 71101 bytes at recorded v8 to 132289 bytes with essentially all of that growth in the review machinery.
advisories.suggestedDisposition: None required of this artifact. Offered for coordinator awareness only.

It does not mark DR-105 or DR-114 SATISFIED, does not seal, does not bind, does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/, does not mint or imply a D-096 (A) grant, does not retarget D-093 or recorded v8, does not edit the subject, does not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, does not edit any frozen v4-v20 verdict, and does not commit. It writes exactly one file, this one.
verdictBasis: The dispatch permits ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. This review returns 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT. The provenance repair that my v20 finding and Codex's HAE20-CX-01 both required is delivered and verified by execution: path existence and digest equality are now required before extraction, the recorded verdict must equal the pinned file's verdict, and the verdict word is tied to the entry's own severities. Running every stated check exactly as written across all thirty lanes from v6 through v20 gives zero failures. The finding is in the one clause the repair added beyond that binding. terminalStatusCheck exempts a file from the terminal-review guard when both status members are absent, naming four lanes as the legacy set, but the trigger is the absence rather than the identity and eight lanes in the artifact's own register take the branch, the four named plus v6/claude2, v6/codex, v7/claude2 and v7/codex. Either the enumeration misstates the corpus or the exemption is open-ended, and the open reading is the same structural-condition-for-an-identity shape that failed at v17 and v18. Codex's requiredRepair asked in terms that legacy handling be explicit rather than inferred, and pinning the legacy set by digest costs nothing because every qualifying file already carries one. The live corpus is clean, which is why this is SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker. I also record, as an advisory rather than a defect, that v21 changes nothing outside the review-bookkeeping machinery and that this is the ninth consecutive generation for which that is true.
